profiles.name: Adolfo Frattesi
profiles.query: "Adolfo Frattesi" Red Scare deportation 1920 portrait photograph
profiles.identity_context:
Adolfo Frattesi was born 1893 in Pergola, Italy. Immigrated to the United States in 1912.

A member of the anarchist Circolo Studi Sociali in Milwaukee, along with his brother Vincenzo Frattesi, sister Maria Nardini, and brother-in-law Pasquale Nardini. Arrested in 1917 following an Italian anarchist “riot” in Milwaukee and initially sentenced to twenty-five years in prison as an accessory to the attempted murder of a police officer. The conviction was later reversed by the Wisconsin Supreme Court. Following his release, rearrested for “teaching or advocating anarchy” and deported to Italy on July 15, 1920. 

Italian authorities do not appear to have placed him under political surveillance after his return.

Adapted from Kenyon Zimmer, Red Scare Deportees (kenyonzimmer.com), compiled from INS deportation case files.

profiles.name: Isso Gartner
profiles.query: "Isso Gartner" Red Scare deportation 1920 portrait photograph
profiles.identity_context:
Isso Gartner was born 1895 in Kassa, Hungary (present-day Košice, Slovakia). Worked as a jeweler. Immigrated to the United States in 1911.

Joined the Socialist Party of America in Baltimore. A conscientious objector, he opposed military conscription during the First World War. Attempted to unionize Baltimore jewelry workers through the International Jewelry Workers Union (AFL). In May 1918 he was arrested on dubious theft charges, sentenced to six months in prison, and later interned as an “alien enemy” at Fort Oglethorpe, Georgia. There he contracted tuberculosis of the hip, forcing him to use crutches. Upon release, Gartner was deported on May 8, 1920 on the unsubstantiated charge that he believed in overthrowing the U.S. government by force.

Adapted from Kenyon Zimmer, Red Scare Deportees (kenyonzimmer.com), compiled from INS deportation case files.

profiles.name: Manya Lansky
profiles.query: "Manya Lansky" Red Scare deportation 1920 portrait photograph
profiles.identity_context:
Manya Lansky was born 1898 in Pieski, Russia (present-day Belarus). Worked as a garment worker. Immigrated to the United States in 1915.

Migrated to the United States for work and soon became an anarchist in New York. She distributed the Union of Russian Workers’ paper Golos Truda. Arrested July 4, 1920 en route to a radical picnic in Cleveland, she was described by an immigration inspector as “the most typical of the usual conception of the anarchistic type that one may have occasion to observe.” She stated, “I am not in sympathy with the leaders of the Soviets, but am in sympathy with the Russian people.” Deported to Russia on February 1, 1921.

profiles.name: S. G. Chestyakov
profiles.query: "S. G. Chestyakov" Red Scare deportation 1920 portrait photograph
profiles.identity_context:
S. G. Chestyakov was born about 1893 in Chernihiv province, Russian Empire (present-day Ukraine). Worked as a laborer. Immigrated to the United States in 1913.

His wife and child remained in Russia when he emigrated. Became a member of the Union of Russian Workers in Donora, Pennsylvania. He was arrested there on September 1, 1920, reportedly after being identified either by an undercover Bureau of Investigation agent or, according to contemporary accounts, betrayed by a fellow URW member. During his arrest, Chestyakov and fellow activist John Sergeyenko were reportedly beaten severely by police, and anarchist literature was found in his possession. Tried and convicted under Pennsylvania’s Sedition Law and sentenced to one year in the Allegheny County Workhouse. Deported on February 26, 1921.
